nodes.label: Handoff 2026-08-03 — Stage 6 closed, Stage 7 review, one vocabulary
/api/cron/dispatch — the scheduler
nodes.rationale: Fails CLOSED without CRON_SECRET (503), so a misconfigured deploy can never become a public mass-mail trigger. Idempotency delegated entirely to email_log_dedup_idx plus Hard Rule 2's insert-first ordering — the insert IS the lock, proven non-vacuous by dropping the index inside a rolled-back transaction.

nodes.label: The `queued` arm is terminal, never 'needs sending'
nodes.rationale: A silent non-send is recoverable via the operator's existing manual button; a duplicate to a regulated practitioner is not. We take the recoverable failure.

nodes.label: Send core extracted to lib/email/eventEmails.ts
nodes.rationale: The Stage 6 plan's 'reuse sendReminderForEvent/sendSurveyInviteForEvent' was not executable: both open with requireStaff(), which throws without a session, and a cron route has none. The old file had been anticipating a session-less pg_cron caller in its comments since Phase 7 — nobody had checked it was possible.

nodes.label: The token layer only reaches components that use it
nodes.rationale: The Stage 6 text-size fix swept text-[Npx] but missed 24 Tailwind default sizes (rem literals) — including every ui/ primitive, so every form control was still unscaled. Fixed by overriding Tailwind's own size tokens once in @theme. Fourth time this class has bitten the codebase; the lesson is not learned until the grep for hand-rolled equivalents is reflexive.

nodes.label: email_log held a table SELECT grant to anon
nodes.rationale: RLS-with-no-policies was the ONLY control in front of recipient_email (PII, Hard Rule 10). Empirically safe, but it inverts the repo's own Hard Rule 11 lesson — RLS is not sufficient, revoke at the grant layer. Same for rate_limits.

nodes.label: seed.sql's blanket grant re-opens revoked table grants
nodes.rationale: Its blanket grant re-grants all tables to the API roles on every db reset, so CI replay-from-zero and future Singapore provisioning would both have produced a database with the PII grant live. The same trap re-opened the events column lock in July; re-assertion added.

nodes.label: The browser instrument wedges hard and lies
nodes.rationale: 0×0 viewports, blank screenshots, dead focus(), and a React-fiber probe suggesting the page had not hydrated when it had — the second recorded instance of that exact false alarm. A fresh tab survives roughly one full-page navigation; document.body.textContent still works when innerText returns 0. Cross-verify with a screenshot before believing a layout is broken.

nodes.label: Full closed-loop verification run + its honest limits
nodes.rationale: create → validate → publish → accredit → register → reminder → attendance → credit issued → freeze trigger blocked a cpd_hours change → survey → analytics → both chains valid. Limits stated: attendance was driven through the same RPCs the Server Action calls, not by clicking the check-in screen (browser auth kept wedging); time was advanced by moving start_time/end_time in the DB.

nodes.label: The plan never mentioned events.deleted_at
nodes.rationale: /events, /checkin and /analytics all filter it and there is a partial index; without the filter the dispatcher mails a soft-deleted event's registrants.

nodes.label: Dead code reported, not deleted
nodes.rationale: components/ui/{select,accordion,toggle}.tsx have 0 importers; lib/{withSecurity,abuseTier,attendeeAuth}.ts are unwired substrate; users.locale and users.display_language are unread. Deleting working components is Ivan's call, not the reviewer's.
